The following figures are
budget allocations

, not fixed market prices. Your model, size, fabric, discounts and delivery determine the actual total. The purpose is to choose priorities within VND 700,000, not promise current product availability.
Option A · Bottom-led

Consider about 45–55% for cargos or wide jeans and 20–25% for a top if needed, with the remainder split between a useful accessory and reserve. Choose compatible shares totaling no more than 100%; this assumes existing shoes.
Option B · Top-led
Consider about 35–45% for a top, corset-inspired garment or jacket, using existing bottoms. Around 20–30% may go to a useful bag or detail; keep the remaining amount unspent or reserved as needed.
Option C · Reuse the base
Keep existing main garments and consider about 40–50% for an outer layer or needed footwear upgrade. Allocate only useful remaining purchases and retain a reserve rather than spending automatically.
Option D · Few foundations
Prioritize a fitting top and bottom with existing sneakers. Do not force boots, a bag and several accessories into the same ceiling at the expense of fit.

01. Baby Tee + Wide Cargos + Sneakers
A neat top contrasts with cargo volume, while familiar sneakers keep the outfit practical. With detailed pockets or straps, compare just one belt or glasses detail.
02. Tank + Wide Jeans + Light Bomber
The tank is a simple base, jeans provide lower volume and the bomber frames the upper shape. Check its actual weight and whether you can remove it comfortably in heat.
03. Fashion Corset Top + Cargos or Jeans + Shoulder Bag
A comfortable structured top defines the upper shape while roomy bottoms keep a streetwear reference. A small useful bag can finish the combination without competing with the trousers.
04. Graphic Tee + Parachute Trousers + Hardware Belt
A graphic tee can take quieter trousers. A partial tuck or waistband-length hem can separate two roomy areas if that is the effect you want.

7. Check Repeat Use Before Buying
Name three outfits you could realistically wear with the new item over the coming month. If it only works in one combination, evaluate it as that narrower purchase rather than assume versatility.
Where can you inspect construction?

For trousers, compare pockets, zip, waistband and drape; for tops, fabric weight, seams and stretch; for bags and belts, closures, edges and hardware. Clear finishing evidence matters more than detail count, but photographs do not prove durability.

Hot weather:
a baby tee or tank, suitable lightweight cargos and sneakers, with manageable hardware. Check actual construction for ventilation.
Rain:
avoid dragging hems and choose appropriate footwear and a bag closure for the conditions. A zip alone does not establish water resistance.
Motorcycle travel:
secure loose drawcords, chains and straps. Outfit styling is not a substitute for suitable riding protection.
Coffee or evening outings:
consider a fashion corset top, bag or glasses for emphasis instead of several extra layers.
Choose pieces for your actual routine rather than a photograph requiring conditions in which you rarely dress.
01 · Copying a complete model set
Top and bottom may need separate sizes; one fitting piece does not establish that the bundle works.
02 · Splitting money equally
This can underfund the main garment while adding unnecessary small details.
03 · Buying boots before checking the clothing gap
A footwear purchase can leave too little for the top or bottom you actually need.
04 · Several competing statements
Detailed cargos, large graphics, chains, a large bag and prominent glasses can all demand attention.
05 · Forgetting the final costs
Delivery, exchanges or required extra items may exceed the ceiling.
06 · Choosing a trend without considering use
An outfit unsuitable for your daily routine may be worn rarely and have a high cost per wear. Compare cost divided by actual or realistic wears; fewer wears do not mean a lower cost per wear.

Can VND 700,000 cover a Baddie outfit?

It can be an update framework when you reuse shoes, tops or bottoms. This is not a verified current basket. If starting with few basics, prioritize fitting main garments and stage footwear or accessories later.
Should the budget prioritize trousers or a top?

Choose the missing function. Cargo, parachute or wide-jean volume can change the silhouette; with suitable bottoms already available, consider a fitted top, comfortable fashion corset top or structured layer.
Should you buy a ready-made Baddie set?
Compare each piece’s measurements, material and independent use first. A shared-size bundle may be less suitable than separate purchases when your top and bottom needs differ.
Which accessories should come first?
A functional belt or shoulder bag may fill more of a gap than several charms. With detailed cargos, one deliberate metal cue may be sufficient. Choose for your wardrobe and use.
